title: Mathematics — DP Entrance

instructions: Answer all questions. Show your working where the question asks for it. Marks for each question are shown in brackets.

**Without using a calculator**, work out  1/3 ÷ 7/6 + 1/5 .

You must show all your working and give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.criteria:
Correct division method: 1/3 ÷ 7/6 = 1/3 × 6/7 = 6/21 = 2/7 (up to 2 marks).
Addition with a common denominator: 2/7 + 1/5 = 10/35 + 7/35 (1 mark).
Final answer 17/35 as a fraction in simplest form (1 mark).
Working must be shown; an unsupported correct answer does not earn full marks.

questions.prompt:
Katy has 5 white flowers, x red flowers and (2x + 1) yellow flowers.
She picks a flower at random.

The probability that it is white is 1/12.

Find the probability that it is yellow.
Calculate  ⁴√(39 1/16)  (the fourth root of 39 1/16).

2.1 × 10⁻¹     0.2̇ (0.2 recurring)     22%     √0.2     24/1000

Write these values in order of size, starting with the smallest.

The interior angle of a regular polygon is 156°.

Work out the number of sides of this polygon.

A car starts its journey by accelerating from rest at a constant rate of 0.7 m/s² for 20 seconds, before reaching a constant speed of 14 m/s.
It then travels at 14 m/s for a distance of 210 m.
The car then decelerates at a constant rate of 1.4 m/s², before coming to a stop.

On the grid, complete the speed–time graph for the car's journey. (The section from 0 to 20 seconds is already drawn.)

[Paper-only drawing task — if you cannot draw, describe in words the lines you would draw, giving the coordinates of the points where each line starts and ends.]
questions.criteria:
Horizontal line at 14 m/s from t = 20 s to t = 35 s (210 m ÷ 14 m/s = 15 s) (up to 2 marks).
Straight deceleration line from (35, 14) to (45, 0) (14 ÷ 1.4 = 10 s) (1 mark).
Accept a clear written description with the correct key points (20, 14) → (35, 14) → (45, 0).

k = 2 × 3² × p³, where p is a prime number greater than 3.

Write 6k² as a product of prime factors in terms of p.

P, Q and R are points on a circle.
ST is a tangent to the circle at R (see diagram — NOT TO SCALE; angle PQR = 65°, angle QPR = 55°, angle QRP = 60°, x° is the angle between chord QR and the tangent RS).

Write down the value of x.
Give a geometrical reason for your answer.
questions.criteria:
x = 55 (1 mark).
Reason: the angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment (alternate segment theorem), i.e. x° = angle QPR (1 mark). Accept clear equivalent wording.

questions.prompt:
P, Q and R are points on a circle and ST is a tangent to the circle at R.
Another tangent from the point S touches the circle at V.

Give a geometrical reason why triangle SVR is isosceles.
questions.criteria: 1 mark for stating that tangents drawn to a circle from the same external point are equal in length, so SV = SR. Accept clear equivalent wording.

Sachin picks a number at random from the first three multiples of 3.
He then picks a number at random from the first three prime numbers.
He adds the two numbers to find a score.

Complete the table (fill in the missing headers and the missing scores, shown as …):

| Prime numbers \\ Multiples of 3 | 3 | … | 9 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **2** | 5 | … | 11 |
| **3** | 6 | … | … |
| **…** | … | … | … |
questions.criteria:
Missing headers: middle multiple of 3 is 6, last prime number is 5.
Completed scores — row 2: 5, 8, 11; row 3: 6, 9, 12; row 5: 8, 11, 14.
2 marks for a fully correct table; 1 mark if at least 5 of the missing entries are correct.

questions.prompt:
Sachin picks a number at random from the first three multiples of 3 (3, 6, 9), then a number at random from the first three prime numbers (2, 3, 5), and adds them to find a score.

Given that the score is even, find the probability that one of the numbers he picks is 9.

Solve.

(5x − 3)(2x + 7) = 0

Give both values: x = ........ or x = ........

Solve the simultaneous equations.
You must show all your working.

y = x² − 9x + 21
y = 2x − 3
questions.criteria:
Equates the expressions: x² − 9x + 21 = 2x − 3 and rearranges to x² − 11x + 24 = 0 (up to 2 marks).
Solves the quadratic, e.g. factorising (x − 3)(x − 8) = 0 (1 mark).
Both solution pairs: x = 3, y = 3 and x = 8, y = 13 (2 marks).
Working must be shown.

questions.prompt:
In this Venn diagram (two overlapping sets A and B inside the universal set ℰ), shade the region  A′ ∪ B′.

[Paper-only shading task — if you cannot shade, describe in words exactly which regions you would shade.]
questions.criteria: 1 mark for shading (or clearly describing) everything except the intersection A ∩ B — i.e. the region outside both circles, A only, and B only are shaded; only the overlap of A and B is left unshaded.

questions.prompt:
In this Venn diagram (three overlapping sets C, D and E inside the universal set ℰ), shade the region  (C ∪ D) ∩ E′.

[Paper-only shading task — if you cannot shade, describe in words exactly which regions you would shade.]
questions.criteria: 1 mark for shading (or clearly describing) the parts of C and D that lie outside E — i.e. all of C ∪ D except any region that is inside E; nothing outside C and D is shaded.

Q2 [3], Q12 [5] and Q19 [2] print one combined mark; per-part splits (1/1/1, 2/1/2, 1/1) preserve totals and follow the official markscheme convention but are an editorial allocation

Source is a Cambridge IGCSE 0580/22/O/N/21 extract with no cover page; durationMinutes=90 taken from the source filename ('1.5 hours') and general instructions were synthesized (not printed in the extract).
Q2 [3] was split into three 1-point parts (2a modal, 2b median, 2c percentage) for auto-marking; the source prints a single [3].
Q12 [5] was split into parts 12a/12b/12c with 2+1+2 points following the standard mark-scheme distribution (13−5n / (n+1)/n / 2^(n−2)); the source prints a single [5] — verify the per-part split.

Q19 [2] was split into two 1-point shading tasks (19a, 19b); Q11 (speed-time graph) and Q19 (Venn shading) are drawing tasks marked paperOnly, with a note asking students to describe their answer in words.
Q16a table completion (including the missing headers 6 and 5) was modeled as open_response since multiple cells must be filled.
Q9 uses a recurring-decimal dot (0.2̇); the answer key compares the printed forms — AI marker should accept equivalent orderings written differently.
Q22 answer key given to 1 d.p. (196.6° and 343.4°); accept equivalent rounding.
Several multi-mark questions with a bare answer line (Q7 [4], Q23 [4], Q21 [3], Q15a [3]) are typed short_answer, so method marks cannot be awarded automatically — teacher review recommended.
Answer keys were derived by solving each question (e.g. Q4 x=79, Q14a x=55, Q18 (3,3) and (8,13)); worth a spot-check against the official mark scheme.
